chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from a man who narrated to him, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about three persons who were on a journey: one of them was in janābah, the second was dead, and the third was without wudu (ablution). The time for salat (prayer) arrived, and they had with them only enough water for one of them. Who should take the water and perform ghusl with it, and what should they do? He said: The junub should perform ghusl, the dead person should be buried, and the one who needs wudu (ablution) should perform tayammum, because ghusl from janābah is an obligation, the ghusl of the dead is a sunnah, and tayammum is permitted for the other.

As for what this report contains—that the ghusl of the dead is a sunnah—it does not contradict what we have said, for several reasons. One of them is that this report is mursal, because Ibn Abī Najrān said, "from a man," and did not mention who he was, and it is possible that he was not trustworthy. Even if it were accepted, what is meant by attributing this ghusl to the sunnah is that its obligation was known through the sunnah, because the Qur'an does not indicate that; rather, we only came to know it through the sunnah. We have already mentioned in the first chapter a narration that among the ghusls there are three obligations, including the ghusl of the dead.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمُ: Dry ablution used as a lawful substitute when water cannot be used.
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: The obligatory salat (prayer) whose time has arrived.
key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: Ritual ghusl, here discussed in relation to janābah and the deceased.
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: A person in a state of janābah requiring ghusl.
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْمَيِّتِ: The washing of the deceased before burial.
key_terms.مُرْسَلٌ: A report with a disconnected sanad/isnad due to an unspecified narrator.

ai.seo_question: When water is only enough for one person, should it be used for ghusl of janābah, ghusl of the deceased, or wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This report addresses a legal ruling concerning limited water during travel when one person requires ghusl for janābah, one deceased person requires washing, and another living person lacks wudu (ablution). It gives priority to the obligatory ghusl of janābah, permits tayammum for the one needing wudu (ablution), and then discusses how the wording about the deceased's ghusl being a sunnah is understood in light of hadith transmission and legal proof through the sunnah.
